params.name: ys
params.let: [x*x - (p+q)*x + p*q for x in range(p-1, p+5)]

stem: The table gives some ordered pairs of the function $f$ where $f(x) = x^2 - {=p+q}x + {=p*q}$ in the interval $[{=p-1}, {=p+4}]$: $f({=p-1}) = {=ys[0]}$, $f({=p}) = {=ys[1]}$, $f({=p+1}) = {=ys[2]}$, $f({=p+2}) = {=ys[3]}$, $f({=p+3}) = {=ys[4]}$, $f({=p+4}) = {=ys[5]}$. Plot these points and draw the curve through them. From the drawing, find the solution set of the equation $x^2 - {=p+q}x + {=p*q} = 0$.
solution: Plot the points $({=p-1}, {=ys[0]})$, $({=p}, {=ys[1]})$, $({=p+1}, {=ys[2]})$, $({=p+2}, {=ys[3]})$, $({=p+3}, {=ys[4]})$, $({=p+4}, {=ys[5]})$ on the coordinate plane and draw a smooth curve through them.
The solutions of the equation are the x-coordinates of the points where the curve meets the x-axis (where $y = 0$).
The curve meets the x-axis at the points $({=p}, 0)$ and $({=q}, 0)$.
Thus, the solution set of the equation is $\{{=p}, {=q}\}$.
notes: Basic: table of values is given; student plots, reads x-intercepts. Roots p<q positive integers, both inside the table range (q-p<=3 so q<=p+3).
